evidence.exact_quote: Contracts_V0 owns only stable cross-surface record envelopes, shared primitive names, and typed payload minima. Domain-specific docs own their behavior and may reference these contracts without copying them. When an owner-specific section and a consumer note disagree, the owner section wins; compatibility/source-lineage tokens remain traceable but do not create peer canon.

items.impact: Implementers have an explicit rule for resolving owner-versus-consumer disagreement without creating peer canon.
items.statement: Contracts_V0 owns shared envelopes and primitive minima, while domain documents own behavior and owner sections override consumer notes.
items.title: Owner-before-consumer precedence is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: Allowed `ConcernRecord.status` values are `active`, `acknowledged`, `resolved`, `dismissed`, and `superseded`. Allowed `resolution_kind` values are `fixed`, `accepted_risk`, `not_reproducible`, `duplicate`, `replaced_by_new_record`, and `not_applicable`. `dismissed` requires a non-empty reason and resolver; `accepted_risk` requires `accepted_risk = true` plus an evidence ref.

Concern actions are authorized by `approval_scope_key`, `actor_ref`, `permission_snapshot_id`, and `allowed_action_ids[]`. User-visible actions such as acknowledge, resolve, dismiss, reopen, or link evidence must produce a typed command response and cannot mutate a concern record by editing projections directly.

items.impact: Concern projections cannot directly mutate durable state, and terminal actions carry explicit validation minima.
items.statement: Concern lifecycle values, resolution values, action authority inputs, and typed command mutation paths are defined.
items.title: Concern lifecycle and authority contract

evidence.exact_quote: Shared governance/runtime records carry `record_id`, `record_kind`, `schema_version`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `owner_ref`, `source_event_refs[]`, `subject_ref`, `status`, `visibility_level`, `redaction_profile`, and `evidence_refs[]`. Records may project into multiple UI or audit surfaces, but the persisted record remains one typed family.

- `created_at_utc`

items.impact: Writers can persist incompatible timestamp, ownership, project-scope, visibility, and lineage shapes while each claims the shared canonical envelope.
items.statement: The document defines two required shared record envelopes with materially different field sets and timestamp names but provides no explicit supersession or normalization mapping between them.
items.title: Shared record envelope is internally split

evidence.exact_quote: Updates with the same `subject_ref`, `concern_category`, and `owner_ref` amend the existing concern while it is active or acknowledged. A terminal concern may be reopened only when its reopen condition is met or when owner/evidence hashes change. Otherwise a new concern id is required.

items.impact: Concurrent validators or operators can race on amendment, reopening, or new-id creation and lose evidence or create duplicate durable concerns.
items.statement: Concern matching and reopen rules omit revision preconditions, atomicity, idempotency keys, and deterministic conflict behavior for simultaneous updates.
items.title: Concern updates lack race semantics

items.impact: Validators can reject dismissal without reason/resolver and accepted-risk closure without the flag and evidence reference.

evidence.exact_quote: - `requested_persona` and `effective_persona` are persisted core runtime identity fields. `_id` variants such as `requested_persona_id` and `effective_persona_id` are retired from canonical contracts and may survive only as migration/source-lineage aliases.

items.impact: Runtime, persistence, and migration code have a stable intent-versus-effective identity vocabulary.

items.title: Requested/effective identity split

evidence.exact_quote: - Runtime, effective-resolution, permission, attempt, usage, and inspector surfaces all project Requested account / Requested binding / Effective account / Switch reason from the same shared runtime identity snapshot.

items.impact: Six named surfaces must disclose the same requested/effective choice and switch rationale, reducing misleading divergence.

evidence.exact_quote: `package-overseer-only` responsibility is bounded local execution supervision, package-level worker dispatch / review cadence, and package-local remediation recommendations. Cross-package promotion, seam governance, durable route identity, and global remediation policy stay outside package-local authority unless the package overseer receives an explicit higher-scope decision.

items.impact: Package-local actors cannot silently promote across packages, govern seams, own routes, or set global remediation policy.
items.statement: Package-overseer authority is local and requires an explicit higher-scope decision for cross-package or global authority.
items.title: Package overseer authority is bounded

evidence.exact_quote: Dispatcher and projection safety are runtime contract concerns. `/domain`, `cmd.runtime`, `cmd.runtime.*`, `correlation_id`, `allowed_action_ids`, and `allowed_action_ids[]` require a trace-through into persisted dispatch/domain events; recovery actions are admitted only when the current blocked episode exposes the corresponding ordered actions. `stale-projection` safety uses a canonical revalidation handshake and disable-with-reason `GUI` behavior before mutation, rather than trusting a stale projection or omitting the disable reason.

items.impact: A stale action set cannot be executed without revalidation, and disabled actions must explain projection health.
items.statement: Mutation through stale projections requires canonical revalidation or disable-with-reason behavior.
items.title: Stale projection actions fail safely

evidence.exact_quote: Canonical persona and account field names must be traceable end to end. `Contracts_V0`, `Contracts_V0.md`, `attempt.started`, usage, storage, auth, and `/effective/provider/account` surfaces must not normatively revive `requested_persona_id` or `effective_persona_id` after this contract forbids them; those names are field-name compatibility aliases only. Provider/runtime/account seams for `OpenCode_Deep_Extraction`, `OpenCode_Coverage_Matrix`, `OpenCode_Deep_Extraction.md`, `OpenCode_Coverage_Matrix.md`, `Media_Generation_and_Capabilities`, `Media_Generation_and_Capabilities.md`, OpenCode, `media.generate`, mid-run, `/effective`, `session-scoped`, disabled-state, `/stream-owner`, `/observe`, server-global, source-verifies, dual-auth-realm, under-specified `/runtime/account`, concurrent-client, capability-change, runtime-correlation, and `GUI` must preserve requested/effective account disclosure and cannot pretend an unobservable server-global stream is a reconnectable, account-owned runtime without explicit evidence.

items.impact: Concurrent clients and network loss can produce duplicated, skipped, or misattributed stream events without a cursor, replay boundary, deduplication key, ownership lease, or reconnect acceptance oracle.
items.statement: The text forbids unsupported reconnectability claims but does not define the reconnect, replay, cursor, deduplication, or concurrent-client protocol needed to make stream recovery implementable and falsifiable.
items.title: Stream reconnect behavior remains undefined

evidence.exact_quote: Runtime attribution uses `package_id`, `run_id`, `node_id`, `attempt_id`, `execution_unit_context_ref`, and `provider_account_ref` where applicable. `package_id` is canonical; `work_package_id` is import/export compatibility only and must normalize before persistence.

Tool and artifact events are runtime contracts when they affect execution, mutation authority, denial recovery, or provider/account routing. `tool.invoked`, `tool.denied`, `/tool`, `/event`, `/event/policy`, `/attempt/actor/account`, and `mutation_capable` records carry the same blocked reason taxonomy and identity envelope as orchestration events. When a tool event intersects Orchestrator execution it is `runtime-attributed`, not merely `analytics-only`, and the record exposes canonical optional refs for `node_id`, `attempt_id`, `lane_id`, `work_package_id`, `feature_seam_id`, `execution_role`, `/runtime`, `/effective`, `effective_account_id`, and `operational_identity`. Tool/artifact linkage must preserve `artifact_id` back to `attempt_id`, resulting artifact refs, and `usage_event_ref` as a secondary `drill-through` anchor rather than the sole evidence trail.

items.impact: Tool and artifact producers can persist the compatibility key that the attribution contract explicitly requires them to normalize away.
items.statement: `package_id` is declared canonical and `work_package_id` compatibility-only, but the later canonical tool-event ref list uses `work_package_id` without an explicit normalization boundary.
items.title: Canonical package identity conflicts in tool events

evidence.exact_quote: Recovery command and wake semantics stay keyed to blocked runtime state. `UI_Command_Catalog.md`, `UI_Command_Catalog`, `HITL`, `cmd.runtime`, `cmd.runtime.*`, and pre-attempt blocked episodes map canonical recovery from `allowed_action_ids[]` to runtime commands; pre-attempt blocks are keyed by `blocked_sequence` instead of fabricated `attempt_id`. The canonical blocked field family is `node.blocked`, `node.unblocked`, `blocked_reason_code`, `blocked_sequence`, ordered `allowed_action_ids`, `allowed_action_ids[]`, `node.prerequisite_resolved`, and the closed `wake_reason` enum `prerequisite_resolved | approval_resolved | clarification_resolved | auth_recovered | startup_recovered | backoff_expired | verification_completed | remediation_resolved | safe_point_restored | capacity_available | replan_applied | watchdog_recheck`; old HITL request examples are compatibility references only when they resolve into that family.

items.impact: Pre-attempt recovery is addressable without fabricated attempts, and wake causes use a closed vocabulary.
items.statement: Blocked episodes, ordered actions, runtime commands, and a closed wake-reason enum form the recovery state contract.
items.title: Blocked recovery is episode-native

evidence.exact_quote: Route validation rejects invalid-combination payloads before any surface-specific open behavior runs. `route_target` requires `project_id` and one primary selector; it must reject a missing primary selector, competing `subject_id` and `object_kind/object_id` selectors, `object_kind` without `object_id`, `object_id` without `object_kind`, `inspector_target` without an object selector, `tab_id` that conflicts with `target_kind`, `line` or `range` inside `route_target`, and any per-surface state inside `route_target`. `/object_id`, `subject_id`, `object_kind`, `object_id`, `target_kind`, `tab_id`, and `inspector_target` are route contract fields only when these selector rules are satisfied.

items.impact: Malformed or ambiguous route payloads have a deterministic rejection boundary before UI behavior executes.
items.statement: Route targets require project scope and one primary selector, with an explicit invalid-combination rejection set.
items.title: Route payload rejection rules are explicit

evidence.exact_quote: Projection health states use one rebuild/scan vocabulary. `/rebuild`, `/scan`, and `/sections` projections use `current` when caught up enough for normal use, `refreshing` when an old committed projection remains visible while refresh or rebuild runs, `stale` when usable for context but not guaranteed to reflect current runtime truth, `degraded` when a projector or scan partially failed or a dependency signal is missing and some fields/sections are less trustworthy, and `unavailable` when the surface contract cannot currently be answered. `Plans/storage-plan.md` and `/storage-plan.md` table-vs-prose conflicts for runtime identity, usage attribution, receipt ownership, and `/projection` ownership resolve to these contract fields rather than to contradictory local tables.

items.impact: Surfaces can distinguish stale-but-visible data, partial projector failure, and total unavailability.
items.statement: Projection health has five shared states with distinct visible and trust meanings.
items.title: Projection health state vocabulary

evidence.exact_quote: Projection health states use one rebuild/scan vocabulary. `/rebuild`, `/scan`, and `/sections` projections use `current` when caught up enough for normal use, `refreshing` when an old committed projection remains visible while refresh or rebuild runs, `stale` when usable for context but not guaranteed to reflect current runtime truth, `degraded` when a projector or scan partially failed or a dependency signal is missing and some fields/sections are less trustworthy, and `unavailable` when the surface contract cannot currently be answered. `Plans/storage-plan.md` and `/storage-plan.md` table-vs-prose conflicts for runtime identity, usage attribution, receipt ownership, and `/projection` ownership resolve to these contract fields rather than to contradictory local tables.

items.impact: Different projectors can label materially different lag as current, undermining mutation gating and cross-surface trust at scale.
items.statement: The phrase `caught up enough for normal use` leaves the current-versus-stale threshold, clock basis, lag metric, and per-surface acceptance oracle to builder discretion.
items.title: Projection freshness threshold is not falsifiable

evidence.exact_quote: `blocked_sequence` is monotonic per `{ run_id, node_id }`, starts at `1`, and increments only when the node transitions from non-blocked to a new blocked episode.

items.impact: Simultaneous blockers, replayed events, or restart recovery can allocate duplicate sequences or create multiple active episodes for the same run and node.
items.statement: The monotonic sequence rule omits atomic allocation, uniqueness enforcement, transition serialization, replay idempotency, and conflict recovery.
items.title: Blocked sequence lacks concurrency semantics

evidence.exact_quote: Attention rows, deep links, search, and palette results share the internal route payload. URLs, in-app actions, `/search/palette` results, deep links, and `resume_url` decode to the same route payload rather than separate link semantics. The canonical internal route payload is separate from command `IDs` and may carry `target_kind`, `project_id?`, `workspace_tab_id?`, `destination_surface`, `destination_tab?`, `focused_run_id?`, `historical_mode?`, `thread_id?`, `wizard_id?`, `object_kind?`, `object_id?`, `record_id?`, `artifact_id?`, `attempt_id?`, `lane_id?`, `worktree_id?`, `filter_payload?`, `inspector_target?`, `scroll_target?`, and `focus_behavior?`.

Route normalization happens before special identifiers enter the canonical route layer. Restore `project_id` first, then route scope such as `focused_run_id` and `thread_id` when present. Normalize every special-case id into `subject_id` or `object_kind` + `object_id`; `subject_id` is not a second generic object taxonomy. Usage routes normalize `usage_event_ref` into `object_kind = usage_event` with the canonical usage event as `object_id`. Graph/detail pivots and `/detail` opens are canonical route restoration, not tab switches plus local state.

items.impact: Producers can emit special-case top-level identifiers that bypass or compete with the canonical selector pair, making validation and round-trip decoding inconsistent.
items.statement: The canonical internal route payload admits multiple direct special-case ids, while the later normalization rule requires every special-case id to become `subject_id` or `object_kind` plus `object_id` before entering the canonical route layer.
items.title: Canonical route payload has competing selector shapes

evidence.exact_quote: Navigation and command migration normalize payload semantics without requiring a hard flag day. Existing user-facing wrapper commands may remain during migration, but their payloads normalize through `route_target` and `OpenSubject`; older payload shapes may be accepted, while new producers and `/docs` emit the canonical normalized target model. Route overrides MUST override target object identity, explicit destination surface when the action names a different surface, and scope required to make the target meaningful, including `project_id`, `thread_id`, `focused_run_id`, an explicitly requested panel, and `/tab`.

items.impact: Public wrappers can remain stable while new producers converge on canonical route and open semantics.
items.statement: Legacy wrapper payloads may be accepted during migration, but canonical normalization and explicit route overrides govern execution.
items.title: Route migration avoids a flag day

evidence.exact_quote: `OpenSubject` subject kinds include `doc:<document_id>` and `artifact:<artifact_id>`. Resolution may end in a workspace-backed source opening, a transient `generated://<artifact_id>` buffer, or a routed non-editor surface. `OpenSubject(subject_id = doc:...)` resolves to workspace-backed source opening; `OpenSubject(subject_id = artifact:...)` resolves to real document source when one exists, otherwise it resolves to transient `generated://<artifact_id>` source opening.

items.impact: Content can open before persistence without turning generated transport into durable identity.
items.statement: OpenSubject resolves document and artifact identities to workspace, transient generated, or routed non-editor realizations.
items.title: Identity-native opening supports transient artifacts

evidence.exact_quote: Approval and restart semantics preserve blocked-state identity across the Contracts, Executor Protocol, and HITL owners. `Plans/Contracts_V0.md`, `/Contracts_V0.md`, `Plans/Executor_Protocol.md`, `/Executor_Protocol.md`, `Plans/human-in-the-loop.md`, and `/human-in-the-loop.md` jointly own the rule that a `waiting_approval` blocked episode exists first-class in `/state`; when an approval prompt surface needs a stable `request_id`, that `request_id` maps 1:1 to the underlying `{ run_id, node_id, blocked_sequence }`. If restart determines an in-flight attempt cannot resume, that attempt transitions to `stale_historical`; if a blocked prerequisite still exists, the existing unresolved blocked episode remains the actionable state.

items.impact: Restart does not fabricate new approval identity or erase an unresolved prerequisite, and non-resumable attempts remain historical.
items.statement: Approval request identity maps to a blocked episode, and restart moves non-resumable attempts to stale history while retaining actionable unresolved blocks.
items.title: Restart preserves blocked episode identity

evidence.exact_quote: Concern-action reversibility is a controlled audit field. Each concern action records actor authority, confirmation, rationale, and one reversibility class from `immediate_undo`, `compensating_action_only`, or `non_reversible`; `compensating_action_only` and `non_reversible` require consequence-specific confirmation before execution.

items.impact: Irreversible or compensation-only concern actions require explicit consequence-aware confirmation and audit data.
items.statement: Concern actions classify reversibility and strengthen confirmation for destructive outcomes.
items.title: Destructive concern actions are guarded

Wizard blocked routing and remediation resolution must not keep competing canonical vocabularies. `wizard.blocked` is grounded in named `route_target`; `resume_url` and `resume_url?` are serialized transport forms only, never a shadow primitive. `remediation.resolved` owns one `resolution` reconciliation: legacy `success | failed | ceiling_exceeded` and current `fixed | superseded | abandoned | replan_required` values must be represented through an explicit compatibility mapping, with `ceiling_exceeded` and `replan_required` retained as named outcomes instead of presenting both lists as independent canonical sets.

Records may project into multiple UI or audit surfaces, but the persisted record remains one typed family.

Downstream identity consumers reconcile to one requested/effective account block owned by `Contracts_V0` / `Contracts_V0.md`, with `Plans/Multi-Account.md` and `/Multi-Account.md` as companion account-policy consumers. That block must expose `/fallback`, `/effective`, and account-switch disclosures, preserve `requested_account_policy`, and define a requested-side concrete account anchor so downstream docs do not improvise requested account selection semantics. `effective_provider_identity` and `/display` labels are audit/display fields, not routing keys, and must not override the canonical account or route identity.

items.impact: Requested/effective account, actor, operational identity, evidence, and history can be over-retained or over-disclosed across projections without enforceable privacy behavior.
items.statement: Although the envelope names visibility and redaction fields, the assigned text does not define redaction-profile semantics, field classification, retention or deletion rules, audience derivation, or safe historical disclosure for identity-bearing records.
items.title: Identity records lack a privacy lifecycle contract

evidence.exact_quote: Graph readability is a route/runtime projection contract before it is a local drawing preference. `Plans/Run_Graph_View.md` consumes zoom-dependent label density: far zoom shows structure/state only, medium zoom shows abbreviated/local labels, near zoom shows full labels and richer local annotations, and selected objects still expose strong detail in the right-side inspector regardless of zoom.

Inspector `/detail` presentations for requested/effective runtime identity use a two-column requested/effective block when both sides are material; controls carry support-status chips, and reason text below the control explains why a requested value was honored, changed, unsupported, or blocked.

items.impact: Keyboard, screen-reader, high-zoom, reduced-vision, bidirectional, and text-expansion users may lose state, support-status, or requested/effective distinctions that sighted English layouts expose.
items.statement: The graph zoom and two-column identity UI contracts omit accessible naming, focus order, non-color status semantics, alternative presentation at large text, localization expansion, and bidirectional layout behavior.
items.title: GUI truth lacks accessibility and localization contracts

evidence.exact_quote: Usage deep links are object routes, not top-level route aliases. Cost or usage rows normalize through `object_kind = usage_event` and `object_id = <canonical usage event id>`; `usage_event_ref` may remain a storage/projection reference, but it must not survive as a top-level route field that bypasses the canonical `object_kind` and `object_id` selector model.

Usage routing treats `usage_event_ref` as canonical when present. `usage-feature` / `usage-feature.md` may retain timestamp or `/run/thread` fallback only as degraded compatibility, not as the preferred routing path when canonical usage identity exists.

items.impact: Usage producers and consumers can disagree on whether `usage_event_ref` is the canonical routing input or merely a storage reference that must be normalized away.
items.statement: One rule forbids `usage_event_ref` as top-level route identity, while another says Usage routing treats it as canonical when present; the input-versus-normalized-identity distinction is not made explicit.
items.title: Usage route identity is self-contradictory

evidence.exact_quote: Approval and dispatch proof stay runtime-command aware. `allowed_action_ids[]` has won at the runtime-command layer, so approval targeting resolves through `blocked_sequence` while any retained `request_id` is lineage or lookup metadata. `GATE-010` must eventually validate more than flat wiring coverage: command wrapper normalization, `route_target` pass-through, `OpenSubject` subject-open binding, and deprecated alias versus stable wrapper semantics are part of the Contracts-owned proof shape.

items.impact: A gate can claim success without executable cases proving route pass-through, subject binding, wrapper normalization, and alias semantics.
items.statement: The text expands GATE-010's intended proof surface but supplies no fixtures, pass/fail predicates, invalid cases, or required receipts for those behaviors.
items.title: GATE-010 remains non-falsifiable
